# ISSUE-29 implementation plan

Reading the relay desk note will file a local receipt and post a bulletin in DEEP FIELD. ECHO and SYSOP will offer distinct scripted BBS lines before and after the read. The feature fits the approved multi-area, detailed profile and 32-hour claim budget. The planning estimate for implementation, focused verification, and review is 6–10 working hours.

## What we know

- The shared loader strictly parses each content kind, sorts paths, checks references and duplicates, and generates the manifest. Both the Node reader and the browser glob already discover nested JSON. The Vite plugin and CLI use the same loader. See `src/content/validate.ts:50`, `:97`, `:142`, `src/content/node.ts:6`, `src/content/browser.ts:3`, `scripts/content-plugin.ts:7`, and `scripts/validate-content.ts:5`.
- Conditions support fact literals, `all`, `any`, and `not`. `checkReferences` gathers flag producers before validating references and already checks dialogue conditions and failure puzzle IDs. See `src/content/conditions.ts:1`, `:15`, `:23`, and `src/content/validate.ts:270`, `:283`, `:348`.
- There are three live fact mutation paths. Puzzle success, episode completion and the archive, map and artifact tools use `createGame`. Door rewards are staged and written with the checkpoint. BBS reads persist stable `message:` and `archive:` keys in `bbsReadMessages`, while archive-tool reads use the separate `archives` field. See `src/puzzle/game.ts:37`, `:72`, `:88`, `src/app/tools.ts:101`, `:113`, `:188`, `src/doors/host.ts:70`, and `src/bbs/progress.ts:60`.
- `createBbsScene` dispatches CONNECT when it mounts and applies successful effects before rendering the next action list. The numbered Messages view uses one visibility selector for the list and READ and already includes status text in the accessible button name. Opening `relay-thread` emits a read key for `relay-note`, with no reply or secret command needed. See `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:28`, `:106`, `src/bbs/bbs.ts:175`, `:237`, `:514`, `:530`, `src/terminal/terminal.ts:118`, and `content/bbs/relay-thread.json:7`.
- `DialogueSource` selects a line using facts, failures, seen IDs, and authored priority. `Game.say` persists seen IDs. The hub's ECHO tool requests a hint or idle line and its reactions are requested at existing action sites. The BBS SYSOP view reads endpoint copy, while ECHO's profile already links to the character ID. See `src/narrative/dialogue.ts:4`, `:18`, `src/puzzle/game.ts:93`, `src/main.ts:37`, `src/app/tools.ts:35`, `:204`, `src/bbs/bbs.ts:392`, `:570`, and `content/bbs/echo-profile.json:5`.
- The repository's native, isolated Linux route uses Codex for development and testing. The product is a static browser app. The separate GitHub Actions `Browser tests` job runs Chromium on Ubuntu, builds the app, and serves the production output under `/signal-lost/` through Playwright request interception. See `.swarm/config.yaml:4`, `:16`, `:63`, `.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:11`, `playwright.config.ts:5`, `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts:3`, and `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:16`.

## What we're assuming

- The existing relay desk note is the best small trigger. It is a public ECHO record on DEEP FIELD, and the planned bulletin can be a local custody receipt without establishing any Chapter 2 story facts. Verify the wording against the character knowledge boundaries in `docs/game-design.md:118` and `:120` during the authored-content review in step 5.
- An additive save v2 extension is sufficient. Its current parser already defaults missing BBS fields and v0/v1 migrations construct v2 data. Verify by reopening a v2 save lacking event fields and the existing completed v1 fixture in steps 2 and 6. See `src/progress/save.ts:37`, `:147`, and `tests/unit/save.test.ts:97`, `:148`.

## Open questions

- Other operating systems, browser engines and agent harnesses are outside the configured verification paths. The configured agent verification path is native Codex on Linux. Step 6 verifies the named browser path in Ubuntu Chromium using the existing workflow. This planner has a read-only checkout, no installed workspace dependencies, and a denied browser capability, so actual DOM and browser results are pending CI.
- Git metadata is absent from the provisioned source snapshot. New paths were checked for absence there. The baseline digest using the TEST_PLAN.md recipe is `e9a80f923cee491edf044937d14dd0d819993c7e78dbb5c6a6e39b9afb2a8d1f`. Step 6 records the implementation source identity from the checkpoint or a content digest, and the coordinator can confirm against the recorded approved base.

## Implementation sequence

1. **Define events and validate their references.** In `src/content/schema.ts:5`, `:160`, `:354`, and `:427`, add `eventSchema`, `NetworkEvent`, and `Content.events`. An event has a stable `id`, a required `when` condition and a nonempty, strict `effects` array. Support `{ "kind": "grant-flag", "flag": "name" }` and `{ "kind": "post-bulletin", "messageId": "id" }`. A bulletin is a BBS message with `eventOnly: true` on a BBS endpoint. It is visible once posted and is marked new until read. In `src/content/conditions.ts:3` and `src/content/schema.ts:8`, add `bbs-read:<message-id>` to condition facts. Keep it read-only by using the previous fact grammar for existing grant fields. In `src/content/validate.ts:50`, `:70`, `:159`, and `:270`, register events, resolve `bbs-read` to BBS message records, and check each post target for existence, kind, and event-only status. Validate endpoint ownership for every event-only message in `checkBbsReferences`. Add event flags to `granted` before checking any conditions. Use the existing loader error format with the event/character file and field, including `when` and `effects.<index>.messageId`. Extend `tests/unit/helpers.ts:3` for the new content kind.
2. **Reject cycles and settle events in one state transition.** In `src/content/validate.ts:270`, add `checkEventCycles` with a producer-to-consumer edge when an event grants a flag mentioned anywhere in another event's `when`. Use `factsIn` so nested and negated references are included. Reject self-edges and cycles among multiple events, with event IDs and a source location. This deliberately rejects a cycle even when a particular branch or a second producer could let it run. Posting adds no immediate condition fact. A player reading that bulletin is a later action. In `src/progress/save.ts:37`, `:79`, `:169`, and `:225`, persist a small `events` slice containing ordered, deduplicated `fired` and `bulletins` ID arrays, defaulting both for older saves, and derive `bbs-read:` facts from stored `message:` keys. Retain the existing version and future-save guard. Implement `settleEvents(events, candidate)` in new `src/progress/events.ts`. At each step select the first eligible unfired event by stable binary ID order, apply its effects in declared order, record its ID, and recheck eligibility until no event qualifies. Expose the IDs fired in that call for tests and connect persistence. Use ordered sets or equivalent for idempotency and assign fresh arrays for changed flags and event state so a staged door save cannot mutate the live state on failure. Reuse `evaluate` and `factsOf`. The loader rejects cycles, and each settlement has at most one iteration per event ID even for a direct caller.
3. **Wire settlement into progress and project bulletins into Messages.** In `src/puzzle/game.ts:72` settle after puzzle and episode facts and before the existing write. In `:88` settle after a nonempty direct grant and before its write. Keep existing grant return values for callers. In `src/doors/host.ts:29` and `:88`, accept an optional candidate-settlement callback and call it after newly earned rewards and before the checkpoint write. Supply it from `src/main.ts:136`. In `src/bbs/progress.ts:48` and `:60`, extend `BbsSnapshot` with event state and let `applyBbsEffect` report whether a previously unseen `message:` key was applied. In `src/main.ts:140`, settle when that report is true and persist the read, history and effects together. In `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:9` and `:28`, invoke an injected connect-settlement callback on the successful offline-to-login transition. The callback settles loaded facts and writes only if an event fires, using the existing save-refused feedback. Preserve BBS in-tab progress on refused writes and door rollback on refused checkpoints. In `src/bbs/bbs.ts:46`, `:175`, `:237`, and `:514`, keep event-only messages out of the ordinary lists, index them by message ID for their own endpoint, and append the posted subset in recorded order to the shared Messages selector. Keep their stable keys in the message lookup so history can resolve titles after a read. Use `text.marked` and add `text.newItem` to `src/content/schema.ts:267` and `content/bbs/interface.json:63` so the list shows `[NEW]` until read and `[READ]` thereafter. Ignore saved bulletin IDs whose records are absent. Existing legacy items keep their `[READ]` and `[UNREAD]` labels and numbering.
4. **Route BBS conversation through character IDs.** In `src/content/schema.ts:147`, `:208`, and `:354`, add a `bbs` line kind, a `TALK` command, and an optional `sysopCharacterId` on endpoints. Allow a character ID or the existing static `sysopGreeting` on an endpoint, with the static greeting available as a legacy endpoint fallback. In `src/content/validate.ts:159` and `:348` check the SYSOP reference and require globally unique line IDs, because `seenLines` stores IDs without a character prefix. Add `createDialogueSources` in `src/narrative/dialogue.ts:18` to build a source per character with the existing selection algorithm. In `src/main.ts:37` use the registry for the named hub ECHO tool and supply a BBS `say(characterId)` callback that requests `bbs` through `Game.say`. Pass it through `src/bbs/door-session.ts:9` into `createBbs` in `src/bbs/bbs.ts:170`. Have `SYSOP` use the endpoint's configured speaker. In `src/bbs/bbs.ts:89` and `:570`, carry the selected profile on the profile route and offer `TALK` when its linked character has BBS lines. Add its label to `content/bbs/interface.json:4`. Keep the SYSOP tone and fictional origin, and label ECHO's exchange as fictional. Existing message bodies, posted documents, and authored receipt selection/replay continue through the message path. Dialogue calls may record seen line IDs. The event evaluator, conditions, reply effects, and unlock logic use saved facts independently of dialogue output.
5. **Add the small example and authoring rules.** Add `content/events/relay-read.json` to grant `flag:relay-note-read` on `bbs-read:relay-note`. Add `content/events/relay-bulletin.json` to post `relay-bulletin` when that flag holds, and `content/bbs/relay-bulletin.json` for the event-only SYSOP bulletin in DEEP FIELD Messages. Set `sysopCharacterId` to `sysop` in `content/bbs/deep-field.json:14` and move the existing greeting verbatim to the baseline BBS line in new `content/characters/sysop.json`. Append only BBS lines to `content/characters/echo.json:315`. Give each speaker a higher-priority BBS line conditional on `flag:relay-note-read`. Keep the example to receipt or custody commentary consistent with the documented voices. Update the relevant subsections in `docs/content-authoring.md:51` and `docs/architecture.md:24` with the condition namespace, effect formats, settlement order, durable `NEW` lifecycle and BBS conversation authoring.
6. **Verify the transition and regressions.** Extend the tests in the handoff and add a named journey to `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts` for the existing workflow. Run the focused source and content checks in TEST_PLAN.md. Capture command, outcome and source identity. Check that the original ECHO dialogue suite and Episode 000 fixture still pass as written.

## HANDOFF

**Dependencies and area boundaries.** Schema, validation, and save state in steps 1–2 provide the contracts consumed by step 3. The character schema and registry in step 4 depend on the same validated facts and feed the BBS presentation and existing hub tool. The example in step 5 exercises both paths. Steps 1–5 precede end-to-end confirmation. Runtime remains the static browser, with pure Node-testable conditions, settlement, and source selection.

**Entry points and symbols.**

- Content and reference checks use `SCHEMAS` and `loadContent` at `src/content/validate.ts:50`, `:70`, `checkBbsReferences` at `:159`, `checkReferences` at `:270`, `FACT_KINDS` at `src/content/conditions.ts:4`, and `Content` at `src/content/schema.ts:427`.
- Progress uses `saveSchema`, `freshSave`, `loadSave`, and `factsOf` at `src/progress/save.ts:37`, `:79`, `:147`, and `:234`. Connect and BBS writes start at `src/main.ts:136` and `createBbsScene.run` at `src/bbs/bbs-view.ts:28`. Other fact writes start at `createGame.attempt/grant` in `src/puzzle/game.ts:72`, `:88`, `applyBbsEffect` at `src/bbs/progress.ts:60`, and `createDoorHost.step` at `src/doors/host.ts:70`.
- Presentation uses `getBbsOffer`, `createBbs`, `screen`, `fromMenu`, and `dispatch` at `src/bbs/bbs.ts:40`, `:170`, `:190`, `:392`, and `:420`. Voice selection enters through `DialogueSource` and `createScriptedDialogue` at `src/narrative/dialogue.ts:14`, `:18`, `Game.say` at `src/puzzle/game.ts:98`, and `createBbsDoorSession` at `src/bbs/door-session.ts:9`.

**Tests and fixtures.** Add `tests/unit/events.test.ts` and `tests/unit/voices.test.ts`. Extend `tests/unit/content.test.ts:174`, `:583`, and `:601` with manifest, cycles and reference cases. Extend `tests/unit/bbs.test.ts:56`, `:88`, and `:195` with speaker routing, read-to-post and view state. Extend `tests/unit/save.test.ts:148` and `:165` for additive v2 defaults and the new derived fact. Extend the staged checkpoint test at `tests/unit/doors.test.ts:282`. Reuse the memory storage patterns, `tests/unit/helpers.ts:3`, and `tests/fixtures/episode-000-complete-v1.json`. Use the BBS journey helpers at `tests/e2e/bbs.spec.ts:11` and `tests/e2e/helpers.ts:5`.

npm test -- tests/unit/events.test.ts tests/unit/voices.test.ts tests/unit/content.test.ts tests/unit/dialogue.test.ts tests/unit/bbs.test.ts tests/unit/save.test.ts tests/unit/doors.test.ts tests/unit/puzzle.test.ts tests/unit/episode.test.ts

**Checked assumptions.** Source and call-site searches confirmed the relay note enters the read ledger from THREAD, BBS archive reads and archive-tool reads are independent, direct fact mutations funnel through the Game or the door host apart from BBS read-key writes, and terminal button names expose label text. # ISSUE-29 test plan

Acceptance indices follow the order in `WORKUNIT.md:24–31`. Unit and content checks use Node 24 on the configured isolated native Linux backend with Codex developer and tester roles (`.swarm/config.yaml:4`, `:16`, `:63`). Browser behavior runs in the static app against the Vite production bundle in Chromium on the Ubuntu GitHub Actions `Browser tests` job. Playwright maps requests under `/signal-lost/` to that build (`.github/workflows/browser-tests.yml:11`, `tests/e2e/global-setup.ts:3`, `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts:16`).

## Acceptance coverage

| Criterion | Concrete cases and expected observations | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **1. Tests prove each event fires exactly once, in deterministic order, for a given fact history, and that a reload neither repeats nor loses it** | In `events.test.ts` feed the same fact updates to two fresh saves with differently ordered event inputs. Include simultaneous eligibility, a downstream event whose ID sorts before its producer, and a repeated grant. Assert the exact ordered event IDs, flags and bulletin IDs at each step. Write and reload a partially settled history before the next fact change, compare with uninterrupted play, then reconnect/reconcile a fully settled reload and assert an empty firing result and identical saved effects. Assert duplicate posting attempts produce one bulletin and an already-read bulletin stays read. In `save.test.ts`, reopen a raw v2 save with a qualifying read and missing event fields and reconcile once, plus verify the v1 default fields. In `events.test.ts`, exercise successful puzzle and episode grants and direct grants through `createGame`, asserting effects in the same persistence call and unchanged grant return values. In `doors.test.ts`, drive a declared reward with an event and inspect persisted checkpoint, reward, and effects together. Force checkpoint refusal and check memory and bytes for all three, then verify retry. | D1. The A6 CI case cross-checks the persisted bulletin in the production app. |
| **2. Event chains settle: validation or evaluation rejects a cycle rather than looping, and a test covers it** | Use `loadContent` in `content.test.ts` to reject a self-produced flag and a two-event cycle through nested conditions, including a negated reference. Assert a diagnostic in the event file/condition with the cycle IDs. Accept a dependency chain and settle it in one call in `events.test.ts`, even when the producer sorts after its consumer. | D1 and D2. |
| **3. Validation rejects events and lines naming unknown records, and flags granted by events count as granted in `checkReferences`** | Extend `content.test.ts` with a valid event manifest entry and with failed fixtures for an unknown fact record in an event condition, an unknown, wrong-kind or ordinary-message bulletin target, a bulletin outside an endpoint, an unknown BBS message condition including an ID of another BBS kind, a missing SYSOP character, an unknown dialogue condition record, and an unknown dialogue failure puzzle. Assert exact source file and relevant field. Verify a flag granted only by an event validates in another event, a BBS condition, and a character line. Remove its producer and expect the ungranted-flag diagnostic. Also prove `bbs-read:` cannot be used as an explicit grant and a duplicate line ID cannot contaminate another speaker's seen state. | D1 and D2. The `content.test.ts` CLI/build tests exercise the shared entry points. |
| **4. Tests prove that two characters given the same facts produce their own distinct lines, and that lines change after a qualifying fact** | In `voices.test.ts`, use the authored character registry and one dialogue state for both speakers. Assert the exact baseline BBS line IDs/text for ECHO and SYSOP and the two distinct higher-priority IDs/text after the same qualifying flag. Assert absent ID lookup is safe. In `bbs.test.ts` run SYSOP and ECHO's profile TALK before and after dispatching the qualifying THREAD action, and verify character selection, tone and line changes. Compare two copies of the same progress transition with dialogue requested from different sources or omitted. Facts, fired IDs, bulletins and unlocks must agree. Speaking may update seen-line memory. | D1. |
| **5. Existing ECHO dialogue tests pass unchanged** | Run `tests/unit/dialogue.test.ts` unchanged. Keep carrier hint escalation, priority, reaction memory and proof against giving away the carrier solution. Run the unchanged Episode 000 replay and check the existing ECHO hint, idle and reaction JSON records against the approved source snapshot. | D1 plus tester source comparison. |
| **6. New items are marked on the next BBS view without using colour alone, and a browser test in the `Browser tests` workflow shows a bulletin appearing after the player reads a qualifying message** | In `bbs.test.ts` drive CONNECT, sign-in, Messages, and open the authored relay thread. Inspect its read key, apply the BBS effect and settle before persisting. The first subsequent Messages view must show one appended bulletin with `[NEW]` in the label. Assert ordinary archive reads and opening the BBS board list alone leave it hidden. Choose the bulletin by its READ action and verify the body, then verify `[READ]` and stable numbering on return. In `bbs.spec.ts` add **posts a new bulletin after reading the relay note**. Seed the existing completed v1 fixture, join, sign in, check absence in Messages, open `BOARDS → GENERAL → Relay desk notes` and assert the visible ECHO note. Return directly to Messages and assert exactly one role button with the bulletin title and literal `[NEW]`. Reload, sign in and verify that same unread listing remains. Click it and verify the authored body, then return to Messages and verify `[READ]`. The completed fixture provides initial board access. The page drives the qualifying read. Existing keyboard/pointer and storage-refusal browser cases continue to run. | D1 for the Node projection and commands, D4 for spec type-checking, and B1 for the actual browser result. |

The normal-save reload guarantee is checked after successful persistence. A separate BBS refusal case verifies the existing in-tab fallback and unchanged stored bytes. A door refusal verifies rollback of checkpoint and effects. Connect starts from loaded progress and evaluates without a rewrite when no new event fires. Inspect the production connect callback and cover already-read v2 connect reconciliation in the focused BBS/save cases.
